summary: Feed s141_double is degraded: 70.1% ERSPAN tunnel encapsulation blinds IDS inspection and 18.3% duplicates waste capacity.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic directly to the IDS without decapsulation. 1344 of 1917 frames (70.1%) still carry ERSPAN outer header, indicating missing 'strip tunnel' policy on the broker egress to the tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload and cannot parse inner Ethernet/IP/TCP headers while encapsulated; 70% of traffic is opaque to signatures and anomaly detection, creating a major detection blind spot.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping ERSPAN at the packet broker exposes the original inner frames so the IDS can decode L2-L7 and apply detection to the 70% currently hidden.

findings.root_cause: Same packets are being delivered twice - consistent with 'double' feed aggregating overlapping SPAN sessions or both sides of a TAP without deduplication. 350 of 1917 packets (18.3%) are duplicates, well above 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU, storage and state-table on duplicate packets, inflates flow/connection counts, risks false positives on threshold signatures and reduces headroom for real traffic analysis.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets within a short time window before the 1G IDS port, eliminating 18% overhead while preserving unique traffic.
